newsitem.title: GERMANY: German banks owed 500 mln dmk by wholesale group.
newsitem.headline: German banks owed 500 mln dmk by wholesale group.

text.p: A consortium of top German banks led by DG Bank and Deutsche Bank AG is owed a total of 500 million marks ($331.9 million) by a group of 2,000 wholesalers on the brink of collapse, DG Bank said Thursday.

The insolvent wholesalers, represented by the Nuernberger Bund Grosseinkauf e.G. co-operative, filed for composition proceedings on Thursday -- thus starting the German system's last defence against bankruptcy.
A DG Bank spokesman told Reuters the banks were making strong efforts to save the Nuremberg group from collapse.
Under composition proceedings, a company negotiates with its creditors to pay back a reduced amount of its debt in order to keep afloat.
DG said the group owed its six main banking partners a total of 500 million marks, of which 200 million marks was due to DG itself.

The spokesman was confirming a report in Germany's Boersen-Zeitung newspaper which said Deutsche Bank, Bankgesellschaft Berlin, BfG Bank, Dresdner Bank, Bayerische Vereinsbank AG and WGZ-Bank were all also involved.
Deutsche Bank confirmed it was involved with the Nuremberg group but declined to name the level of its exposure. Earlier, Boersen-Zeitung said Deutsche Bank's share of the debt was 120 million marks.
